This report outlines the destination vehicular way-finding guidelines for civic, cultural, visitor and recreational attractions in the city.
A legibility criteria for tourist destinations, applicable sign types, and the application process are established.
The guidelines were developed in response to requests received from a variety of destinations for way-finding signage to direct drivers to their location.
The administration does not currently have guidelines for destination vehicular way-finding and has previously approved or denied requests on a case-by-case basis.
This resulted in inconsistent sign design, placement, frequency, and condition.
To reduce sign clutter, provide consistent messaging to drivers, align with national guidelines and best practices and ensure an equitable opportunity to receive way-finding signage.
The destination vehicular way-finding guidelines shown in this report were created.
Three stakeholder engagement events were held during the development of the guidelines to obtain feedback.

Stakeholders were generally supportive of the guidelines and the more transparent process, but a few stakeholders expressed concerns about the timeline of implementation, requirements for parking, attendance, numbers, and the exclusion of shopping centers as destinations.
If the guidelines are approved in principle, the administration will inform destinations about the guidelines and the application process for internal street network signs.
Finalized the implementation plan, including additional stakeholder engagement, and prepare funding request for the implementation in future multi-year business plan and budget submissions.
